content.text: {"relation":"DIVERGENT","consensus_summary":"A name primarily represents the bearer’s identity or person, especially the bearer’s character, authority, presence, and reputation; covenantal belonging is a secondary contextual use.","book_summary":"The Name is identified as the covenant itself, conceived through marriage: being called by God’s name means entering covenantal belonging, protection under his wing, and obligation to his commandments.","consensus_core_identification":"Name = the identity or person of its bearer.","book_core_identification":"Name = the covenant relationship itself.","core_relation":"CONTRADICTS","extension_relation":"PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION","boundary_disagreement":"The book reclassifies covenantal and marital-belonging passages as expressing the essential meaning of “name,” while the consensus treats these as contextual consequences or secondary uses of a name that fundamentally represents its bearer.
